text:
maria (Support): ping — Acme Mobile reporting intermittent 429s for several hours. They say per-second traffic is low but roughly ~5% of responses are 429. Rollout of AcmeMobileSDK/2.4.0 happened ~02:00 UTC. Anyone seen similar symptoms?
acme-mobile (Customer): example request and response:
```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***
User-Agent: AcmeMobileSDK/2.4.0 (iOS)
X-Request-Id: 9f2b7a3c
```
429 body: {"error":"quota_exceeded","message":"requests per minute exceeded"}
maria (Support): tracing x-request-id 9f2b7a3c now.
ratebot: trace 9f2b7a3c -> us-east-1-dedicated-pool-3, backend=i-0abc1234, ts=2025-10-18T03:42:11Z, quota_bucket=customer:acme_mobile:minute used=1200 allowed=1000
devon (SRE): that minute usage explains the 429s server-side. But Acme's own metrics show ~4-8 rps from clients (240-480 rpm). There's a disconnect.
devon (SRE): pulling minute-aligned series for their API key (12h)
Devon (SRE): sample minute_bucket_used: [300, 280, 290, 980, 1015, 995, 1020, 990]
Devon (SRE): 1s_peak samples: [6, 7, 5, 6, 8, 7]
sophie (Platform Eng): looks like most seconds are low, but a tight spike injects a large chunk into the same minute. Could be devices flushing queued requests simultaneously.
acme-mobile (Customer): we did change reconnect behavior in 2.4.0. snippet:
```
func networkBecameReachable() {
  queue.flushAll()
}
```
no jitter/backoff — hm.
devon (SRE): that explains it. If many clients restore connectivity at similar times (carrier handover, morning wifi reconnect), they all flush and the minute bucket fills fast even though per-second peaks stay modest.
sophie (Platform Eng): our histograms show ~70% of that minute's traffic hits within a 3-5s window. that's sufficient to exceed minute quota.
maria (Support): mitigation options:
- immediate: temporary per-key minute quota increase (24h) while they ship a fix.
- platform-side: enable short-term smoothing for this key (spillover/leaky-bucket) to spread excess across seconds.
- customer fix: add jitter and batch caps on queued flush.
raj (Account Exec): customer prefers a quick quota bump to avoid revenue loss. can support grant a temporary increase?
devon (SRE): i can apply a scoped quota bump on their api key only. will set minute_quota=2400 for 24h and monitor. no global changes.
ratebot: policy update applied: customer:acme_mobile minute_quota=2400 until 2025-10-19T04:00:00Z by devon
acme-mobile (Customer): after the bump 429s dropped to ~0 within 2 minutes. huge improvement, thanks.
sophie (Platform Eng): long-term proposals:
- RFC: auto-detect "flush-burst" patterns and enable per-key smoothing heuristics.
- docs/sdk: recommend jitter + cap when flushing queued requests.
sophie (Platform Eng): recommended SDK rules:
- before flush, sleep(rand(0, jitter_ms)) where jitter_ms maybe 0-2000ms
- cap per-device flush batch size to 3-5 requests and stagger batches by 200-500ms
maria (Support): can eng run a repro so platform folks can test smoothing strategies?
sophie (Platform Eng): quick repro (bash):
```
# spawn N clients that hold requests and flush together
for i in $(seq 1 2000); do
  (sleep $((RANDOM%5)); printf "POST /v1/generate ...\\n" | nc api.redwood.example 443) &
done
# then trigger flush simultaneously and watch minute_bucket metrics
```
sophie (Platform Eng): adjust N and sleep to get the 3-5s concentration.
devon (SRE): adding a synthetic to our harness to model queued-flush bursts so we can measure smoothing effectiveness and latency impact.
maria (Support): action items:
- devon (SRE): applied quota bump and will schedule removal, monitor metrics and set rollback triggers. (assigned)
- sophie (Platform Eng): open RFC for smoothing heuristics + update best-practices doc and repro script. (assigned)
- acme-mobile (Customer): ship SDK 2.4.1 with jitter + batch caps and share rollout plan. (customer)
- support: follow up in 24h and close thread if stable. (assigned)
acme-mobile (Customer): we'll push 2.4.1 to TestFlight in ~7h, roll out 10% -> 100% over 6h and report any issues.
devon (SRE): rollback plan: when the bump expires, if minute_bucket_used > 1000 sustained we'll enable a short soft-rate-limit for that key returning 429 + Retry-After and a link to guidance. monitoring alerts set.
ratebot: reminder: quota bump expires 2025-10-19T04:00:00Z
maria (Support): thanks all for rapid triage. i'll keep the customer updated and close after 24h if green. :clap:
acme-mobile (Customer): thanks everyone 499
